images.seen: Near East, Egypt, Elam, Anau, Indus and the Doab/Ahar-Banas cultures are in plausible places; compiled adds the Isin, Larsa, Eshnunna, Qatna and Assur discs Cliopatria lacks; Indus is drawn at the full Mature extent (3,027 cells, Baluchistan to Gujarat), which the dossier meant to cut to the Late Harappan shape at -1900.

Mari (three discs along the Euphrates), Yamhad, Qatna, Assur and Shekhna, Eshnunna (Kirkuk, Diyala, Rapiqum), Babylonia, Isin, Larsa (to the Gulf head), Elam: nothing outside its region, no holes; one Isin patch sits east of Larsa (leftover of Cliopatria's Sumerian outline minus the Lagash circle).
27 states, all in their own regions, no stray cells; Anau has a one-cell speckle at 54.5 E 37 N, harmless.
Longshan gone, Xia as a small disc in Henan, Jeulmun and Jomon as Cliopatria draws them; the Shandong land of the Longshan (868 cells) becomes nobody's, with no Yueshi dossier to take it.

Indus now the Late Harappan shape (1,389 cells: Punjab, Sindh corridor, Gujarat, Haryana and Delhi), Baluchistan uplands and coasts dropped as the dossier's -1900 loss event intends; Ochre Coloured Pottery and Ahar-Banas unchanged.

issues.what: Indus Valley Civilisation drawn at the full Mature extent (3,027 cells) for -1900..-1801: keyframe indus-valley-civilization_-2000 has no `to`, so it stays alive to Cliopatria's row end (-1801) and, unioned with the -1900 Late Harappan keyframe, undoes the dossier's own -1900 loss event (1,638 cells; a snap in the packet). Its note says it holds only -2000..-1901; the page dates the Mature phase 2600-1900 BC and the Late Harappan 1900-1300 BCE.

Eshnunna snap at -1828 (55 cells): the keyframe adds the Diyala region and Tutub, but ledger/5 resolves only Kirkuk. Ipiq-Adad II 'to consolidate the Diyala region, he defeated Sin-abushu' and 'annexed Uzarlulu and Tutub' in the same campaign as Arrapha (c. 1828).

Lim dynasty of Mari snap at -1830 (53 cells): the keyframe draws Terqa and Tuttul from -1830, but the dossier's ledger/1 gives them at -1810, and the Yahdun-Lim page (reign c. 1820 - c. 1797, rebellion of the Yaminites 'centered at Tuttul') shows Tuttul was not held under Yaggid-Lim (no territory or dates given for him). The keyframe now starts at -1810; -1830..-1811 is Mari alone.

Longshan culture ends at -1900 and its Shandong land (868 cells) plus the Shanxi/Luoyang centre are given to 'erlitou-culture' and the Yueshi culture, neither of which has a dossier; the land is nobody's. The Xia dossier draws only a small Luoyang/Zhengzhou area until -1750.
Assyria snap at -1808 (12 cells): the keyframe draws Assur at 45 km, the ledger at 35 km; Ekallatum is the difference. Too small to matter.
Minoan civilization snap at -1900 (11 cells removed): the found event draws all of Crete (27 cells), the Cliopatria keyframe 16 of them. No neighbour, no effect on the picture.

Size-rule conflicts babylonia/isin (19 cell-years, -1894) and eshnunna/isin (9, -1900): the smaller state wins; Isin's claim there is Cliopatria's blunt Sumerian outline, and Babylonia's tract around Babylon and Eshnunna's lower Diyala are the better readings.

Isin keeps a 29-cell patch around 47-48 E 31 N, east of Larsa, as the remainder of Cliopatria's Sumerian outline once the Larsa, Ur, Lagash and Uruk circles are cut out; the pages give Isin no land there but also give no border for Lagash province.

Middle Kingdom of Egypt: Sinai gained at -1839 (109 cells, dossier-dated, confidence-low) and the Kerma contest -1873..-1863 (24 cells) rest on the dossier's own dated events; nothing in the picture contradicts them.

patch_check: all applied (--check-patch: 3 ok, 0 rejected; --trial: events/0, keyframe_overrides/0 and /1 applied; keyframe snaps 6 -> 3 (Indus 1,638, Eshnunna -1828 and Mari -1830 gone); conflicts unchanged; end anchor m1800: 1,652 cells change owner, Indus 3,027 -> 1,389)

dossier_requests.what: New dossier for the Yueshi culture, c. -1900..-1500, on Shandong (core: the Tai-Yi Mountains of central Shandong), eastern Henan and north Jiangsu, successor of the Longshan culture, replaced by the Erligang culture.
dossier_requests.why: Longshan culture ends at -1900 and leaves 868 Shandong cells to nobody until the Shang; the Longshan ledger/3 itself names the Yueshi as its Shandong successor.

dossier_requests.what: Give keyframe indus-valley-civilization_-2000 an explicit `to` of -1901 (covered by keyframe_overrides/0 until the dossier is edited).
dossier_requests.why: Without it the keyframe stays alive to -1801 and keeps the Mature shape through the Late Harappan phase.

dossier_requests.what: Start keyframe lim-dynasty-of-mari_-1830 at -1810 (covered by keyframe_overrides/1 until the dossier is edited).
dossier_requests.why: The ledger dates the Terqa and Tuttul gain to -1810; the keyframe drew it from -1830.

problems: cross-window: keyframe_overrides/0 overrides indus-valley-civilization_-2000 (years -2000..-1901), which starts in m2000-m1901; only `to` changes (-1801 to -1901), so no cell of that window changes. If the m2000-m1901 agent overrides the same shape_id, its file wins in window order and mine is skipped; it must then also set `to` -1901.

cross-window: the end anchor m1800 changes (Indus 3,027 -> 1,389 cells, Eshnunna +5); the m1800-m1701 agent's Indus -1800 snap of 1,638 cells (their report, issue 'left: pages silent') should vanish after the next compile; I did not trial that window.

the trial's comparison with the published draft counts 3 conflict pairs, 30 cell-years, against the packet's 2 pairs, 28, because of dossier edits since the 1 Nov compile; my patch does not change them.
no hierarchy: rows found wrong in this window (the packet lists none for it).
